messages:

Date: Mon, 20 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Marketplace procurement: technical + governance questionnaire

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for speaking with Raj and me last week. As we kickoff our procurement review for vendors to appear in our SaaS marketplace catalog, Procurement has a short set of follow-ups specific to AWS/Azure/GCP marketplace listing requirements and seller readiness. Our security and procurement teams want a single consolidated artifact that covers: seller registration status, billing/metering approach for each cloud marketplace, compliance evidence (SOC2/ISO), private offer capability, data residency options, and how you handle license & contract delivery (SaaS contract vs. marketplace terms).

Can you:
- Confirm which marketplaces Redwood is currently listed on (AWS, Azure, GCP) and include listing IDs where available?
- Provide the technical readiness matrix by marketplace (metering mechanism, SaaS vs. AMI/container, required integrations like CloudFormation/ARM templates, GCP deployment manager notes).
- Attach any procurement artifacts (SOC2, PII data flow diagrams, or vendor registration proofs).

We're aiming to finalize vendor onboarding by 2028-03-05. If you can send a single consolidated reply with the matrix and any attachments by EOD Wed (2028-02-22) that would keep us on schedule.

Thanks,
Susie
Procurement Manager, FinTechCo

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Susie Lam <susie.lam@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Feb 2028 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Marketplace procurement: technical + governance questionnaire

Hi Susie — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a draft technical readiness matrix and our SOC2 summary for your team (see attachments). Quick notes up front so you have context while you review the spreadsheet:

- Marketplace coverage: Redwood currently supports listings on AWS Marketplace (SaaS contracts / private offers), Microsoft Azure Marketplace (SaaS), and Google Cloud Marketplace (SaaS via GCP Marketplace SaaS contracts). We include private-offer and metered billing support on AWS and GCP; Azure supports private listings through Microsoft Seller Center.
- Metering/billing: For AWS and GCP we support usage-based metering using the marketplaces' SaaS metering APIs. We also offer flat-rate subscriptions for marketplace storefronts where metered billing isn't preferred.
- Deployment model: All marketplaces use our managed SaaS listing (no AMI/VM images). For customers that require on-prem, we provide a Private deployment package (air-gapped installer + licensing) — that path is separate from marketplace procurement.
- Contracting: We can execute via marketplace terms (preferred for frictionless procurement) or via a private offer / marketplace contract with a DocuSign equity-ready master services agreement.

Marissa and Karthik — looped you both for technical and GTM details. I plan to add clarifying rows in the matrix for: data region options per cloud, expected provisioning lead time for private offers, and post-sale support escalation flows.

Deliverables attached: redwood-marketplace-technical-matrix.xlsx, soc2-type2-summary-2027.pdf, aws-seller-registration-guide.pdf. Will follow up with any clarifications on Wednesday.

Best,
Evelyn
Director, Strategic GTM Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Feb 2028 08:10:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Marketplace procurement: technical + governance questionnaire

Susie — a few technical clarifications from my side based on the matrix: 

1) Metering details (AWS/GCP):
   - AWS SaaS metering: we use AWS Marketplace SaaS Metering APIs. Meter granularity is per-session-minute or per-token-unit (we can map tokens to consumption units for consistent billing).
   - GCP SaaS metering: uses GCP Entitlements + Usage Reporting endpoints; we can emit usage summaries hourly.

2) Authentication & provisioning:
   - Marketplace provisioning triggers our onboarding job which creates a dedicated tenant and issues initial API keys. For enterprise buyers that require SCIM or SSO via SAML/OIDC, we support both and can configure tenant-level SCIM provisioning within 3–5 business days post-purchase.

3) Data residency / encryption:
   - We support region pinning on Dedicated and Private deployments. For hosted marketplace SaaS we store customer data in the region selected at signup (US East / US West / EU West). Data at rest is encrypted (AES-256) and in transit via TLS 1.2+. KMS integration available for Dedicated/Private.

4) Support SLAs & billing reconciliation:
   - Marketplace purchases can be backed by standard support (48-hour response) or premium (4-hour response + named TAM) per the enterprise offer. Billing reconciliation exports (CSV) are available for buyers and can be mapped to internal invoice IDs.

I'll annotate the spreadsheet with example entitlement IDs and a sample private-offer flow diagram. If you need a short call to walk the procurement team through the matrix, happy to set one up.

- Marissa
Senior Product Manager, Partnerships

Thanks, team — this is very helpful. A couple quick follow-ups after review with Legal & Cloud Ops: 

1) Private Offer timing: can Redwood commit to a 5-business-day turnaround from receiving our DocuSign signature for a private offer (creation + QA + entitlement mapping)? We need this in our procurement SLA table.
2) Metering granularity: we prefer per-1000-token billing tiers for predictability. Can you include an example mapping from token counts to the metered unit in the matrix?
3) SOC2 evidence: Legal asked for a short controls mapping doc (SOC2 control -> evidence URL/page). Can you provide that as an appendix to the SOC2 PDF?

If you can send updated matrix + a short controls mapping by EOD Friday (2028-02-24) that would be ideal. Otherwise, let us know when the earliest delivery will be.

Appreciate the fast responses.
Raj
